bull.last: AMD: argues long. AMD is trading at a 25.25% discount to its 52-week high of $658.52, creating a high-asymmetry long setup ahead of the 2026-11-03 earnings print. The stock has corrected -24.2% over 20 days, bringing the price ($492.26) well below the 20-day SMA ($554.34) and 50-day SMA ($548.87), which historically marks a mean-reversion entry point given the long-term uptrend (price is +19.1% above the 200-day SMA of $412.99). Fundamental momentum remains robust with 124.33% YoY EPS growth and 50.11% revenue growth in the latest quarter, supported by a clean balance sheet with only 0.048 debt-to-equity. The reversion signal record shows a 64% win rate with an average return of 0.49R, outperforming the momentum signal's 33% win rate, suggesting that buying this dip is statistically superior to chasing momentum. With a mean analyst target of $649.38 (31.9% upside) and zero sell ratings, the downside risk is capped by the 200-day SMA, while the upside is open to the prior high.

bear.last: SHOP: The bull's thesis is dangerously naive because it ignores the violent post-earnings breakdown: SHOP is trading 12.9% below its 50-day SMA and has already broken below the 20-day low of $153.33 on 2.23x volume, confirming a distribution event rather than a buying opportunity. The 'oversold' RSI of 36 is a trap; the stock is down 11.1% in just 5 days, indicating strong downward momentum that mean-reversion strategies historically fail to catch in high-beta names (Beta 2.74). The valuation remains extreme at 106x P/E and 15.5x P/S, meaning the market is punishing the stock for a growth deceleration narrative or macro fears, not just technicals. With implied volatility at 73% and a put/call ratio of 1.41, the options market is pricing in significant downside risk, and the Kronos forecast shows only a 50% probability of an up move, offering no statistical edge for a long entry.
